paper_metadata.title: Grover search algorithm with Rydberg-blockaded atoms: Quantum Monte Carlo simulations

summary: The paper numerically simulates a Rydberg‑blockade implementation of Grover’s algorithm for registers up to k = 4 atoms (database size N ≤ 16) using Monte‑Carlo wavefunction simulations with realistic decay (Γr up to 10^5 s^-1) and dephasing (γr up to 10^5 s^-1). Success probabilities are evaluated over 200 trajectories and shown to degrade with increasing decoherence, while higher Rydberg laser Rabi frequencies (|Ωl| = 2π×2 MHz vs 0.5 MHz) improve performance. Two interaction architectures are compared: direct register‑register blockade and ancilla‑mediated blockade.

experiments.description: Simulation study of Grover search implemented with Rydberg-blockaded atoms for register sizes k=2,3,4 under realistic decay/dephasing, comparing two blockade configurations (direct register-register blockade and ancilla-mediated blockade).

algorithm.parameter_initialization: Register initialized to equal superposition using U−π/2(π/2) on all atoms initially in |0⟩

problem_formulation.encoding_details: k qubits encoded in k Rydberg-blockaded atoms; each computational basis state corresponds to one database element x ∈ {0,1}^k
problem_formulation.objective_function: Grover search for a marked bitstring xm = b0b1...bk−1 by phase-flipping the marked state and applying inversion about the mean
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Rydberg blockade enforces conditional oracle and Grover operations; no penalty formulation

problem_instance.description: Unstructured search over a database of size N = 2^k for one marked element xm

dataset_specification.description: Marked inputs tested include 01, 010, 0101 and comparison cases such as 00, 000, 0000 and 11, 111, 1111

problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Quantum stochastic (Monte Carlo) wavefunction simulations; probabilities averaged over 200 independent trajectories; success probability plotted versus Grover iteration number

noise_model.noise_type: Lindblad decay and dephasing; quantum jump / Monte Carlo wavefunction simulation

implementation_details.classical_solver: Monte Carlo wavefunction simulation on classical computer
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Select marked bitstring and set pulse sequence for oracle/Grover iterations; apply Stark shifts to selectively detune atoms from global microwave field
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Measure all register atoms; interpret non-|0⟩ outcome as bit 1 or atom loss |o⟩; average success probabilities over trajectories

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: success probability versus iteration number; peaks after a few Grover iterations depending on noise

speedup_claims.conditions: Grover search over an unstructured database of size N = 2^k
speedup_claims.caveats: This is the standard Grover scaling claim; the paper reports noisy simulations and does not benchmark against a classical runtime.

advantage_assessment.crossover_size: Not analyzed; simulations only cover k ≤ 4 (N ≤ 16)
advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Would require large neutral‑atom registers with high‑fidelity Rydberg blockade gates and many Grover iterations scaling as O(sqrt(N)); far beyond the k ≤ 4 simulated system.
limiting_factors: Only simulated systems up to 4 qubits
Significant decoherence from Rydberg decay and dephasing

notes: hardware.type inferred as real_qpu_neutral_atom because the paper describes a neutral-atom Rydberg-blockade implementation, but the reported results are classical Monte Carlo simulations rather than a physical device run.
circuit_depth not explicitly reported; only the number of Grover iterations and pulse sequence structure are described.
num_shots inferred from '200 independent trajectories' used for averaging.
The paper discusses the standard Grover quadratic speedup theoretically but performs only noisy classical simulations and does not demonstrate computational advantage over classical search.

experiments.description: Simulation of Grover search using Rydberg‑blockaded atoms with direct register–register blockade interactions (no ancilla), evaluating success probability vs. iteration number under different decay and dephasing parameters.

algorithm.variant: Rydberg blockade Grover implementation (direct register‑register interaction, Eq. 4)

key_results: Success probability peaks after a few Grover iterations and degrades with increasing Rydberg decay (Γr up to 10^5 s^-1) and dephasing (γr up to 10^5 s^-1).
Higher Rydberg laser Rabi frequency (|Ωl| = 2π × 2 MHz vs 0.5 MHz) improves robustness to decoherence.

experiments.description: Simulation of Grover search using an ancilla‑mediated Rydberg blockade configuration where register atoms interact only with an ancilla atom (Eq. 5).

algorithm.variant: Rydberg blockade Grover implementation with ancilla atom

key_results: Simulated for register sizes k = 2, 3, 4 plus one ancilla qubit.
Performance is broadly similar to the direct‑interaction scheme but becomes worse when Rydberg decay is very strong because multiple register atoms may be excited simultaneously.
Decoherence parameters strongly limit achievable success probability.
